Why This Is Asked
- Tests practical multi-homing and policy-based routing
- Checks persistence across reboot and NM integration

Key Concepts
- iproute2: routing tables, fwmark rules
- iptables/nftables: packet marking; NetworkManager persistence
- SSH vs web traffic separation; DNS considerations

Code Example
```javascript
// 1) define routing tables
echo '100 SSH' >> /etc/iproute2/rt_tables
echo '101 WEB' >> /etc/iproute2/rt_tables

// 2) mark SSH to route via eth1
iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j MARK --set-mark 1
ip rule add fwmark 1 table SSH
ip route add default via 10.1.0.1 dev eth1 table SSH

// 3) mark HTTP/HTTPS to route via eth0
iptables -t mangle -A OUTPUT -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443 -j MARK --set-mark 2
ip rule add fwmark 2 table WEB
ip route add default via 203.0.113.1 dev eth0 table WEB
```

- How would you restrict SSH routing to management IPs only?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests core RHCSA beginner skills: user creation and permissions, small script, systemd service basics, log management with rotation, and boot-time enablement.

## Key Concepts
- Systemd service fundamentals
- Non-login user handling
- File permissions and ownership
- Log rotation basics

## Code Example
```bash
# Create user
sudo useradd -r -s /sbin/nologin -d /var/empty hello
# Prepare script
sudo mkdir -p /opt/hello-day
sudo tee /opt/hello-day/print.sh <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
echo "Hello from $(date) on $(hostname)" >> /var/log/hello-day.log
SH
sudo chmod +x /opt/hello-day/print.sh
sudo mkdir -p /var/log/hello-day
sudo chown hello:hello /var/log/hello-day.log
# systemd service
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/hello-day.service <<'SERVICE'
[Unit]
Description=Hello Day Service
[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=hello
ExecStart=/opt/hello-day/print.sh
SERVICE
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now hello-day.service
# logrotate
sudo tee /etc/logrotate.d/hello-day <<'LOG'
/var/log/hello-day.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  missingok
  notifempty
  create 0640 hello hello
  copytruncate
}
LOG
```
